params.title: Five habits
params.line: Zodl was called Zashi in older guides

narration: By the end of this video, you will know five habits that keep your payments private.

segments.name: e5-habits
narration: One. Keep your ZEC shielded. If ZEC lands at your t1 address, shield it.
Two. Do not shield an amount and then send the same amount to a transparent address soon after. That pattern is easy to spot.

segments.name: e5-habits-more
narration: Three. Turn on Tor Protection. It sends your connection through the Tor network for extra privacy. Open Advanced Settings, tap Tor Protection, choose Enable, then tap Save changes.
Four. Guard your recovery phrase. Keep it on paper. Anyone who asks for it is trying to scam you.
Five. Check the address before you send. A t1 address is public. If you are not sure, use the address checker on the site.

segments.name: e5-guard
narration: Test yourself with Phrase Guard on the site. Six quick questions, safe or scam.

segments.name: e5-end

params.line: Zodl will never ask for your recovery phrase

narration: Need help? Go to support.zodl.com. Zodl will never ask for your recovery phrase. That is the whole path, zero to shielded.

upload.title: Stay private: five habits | Zero to Shielded 5
upload.description:
Five habits that keep your Zcash payments private. This is episode 5 of Zero to Shielded, the last step on the path.

Watch the series and tick your progress: https://zero-to-shielded.vercel.app

Shielded means the amount, the sender and the receiver are encrypted on the blockchain. Transparent means public on the blockchain, like Bitcoin.

The five habits:
1. Keep your ZEC shielded. If ZEC lands at your t1 address, shield it.
2. Do not shield an amount and then send the same amount to a transparent address soon after. That pattern is easy to spot.
3. Turn on Tor Protection. Open Advanced Settings, tap Tor Protection, choose Enable, then tap Save changes.
4. Guard your recovery phrase, the 24 words that bring your wallet back. Keep it on paper. Anyone who asks for it is trying to scam you.
5. Check the address before you send. A t1 address is public. If you are not sure, use the address checker on the site.

Then test yourself with Phrase Guard on the site: six quick questions, safe or scam.

Chapters:
{chapters}

Wallet steps are shown as labelled step diagrams with the exact button names from the Zodl app, not as drawings of the app. Every fact is sourced in docs/FACTS.md. No recovery phrase appears on screen.

Zodl was called Zashi in older guides.

Zodl will never ask for your recovery phrase.

Zodl: https://zodl.com/
Zodl support: https://support.zodl.com/

Video, narration and script: CC BY-ND 4.0. Repost with credit, no edits.

Scripts, narration and editing were produced with AI assistance (Kiro). Narration is a synthesised voice (Kokoro, Apache-2.0). Music is original and generated in code.
